study: Does the sealed RGB target window lower-bound the amodal box projection?
cohort: All 416 distinct ordinary frames from the locked C_E_Qsize recording confirmation. Report all, by platform, the 288 Validation frames, the overlapping 224 recording-separated frames, the TRAIN extension and selected-region versus original fallbacks. This is an exposed development cohort.
stage_1: No model calls, training, box edits or optimizer in the prerequisite audit. Read sealed Qwen 0-1000 target rectangles and frozen H boxes. Seal all label-free projected rectangles, availability and violations first. Only then use the exact target slot from the ordinary labels, task IoU and diagnostic label fields. No FINAL.
projection: Use the current calibrated raw sensor-to-camera transform, original image size and the existing eight-corner upright-box projection/visible-image clipping. Use each archived camera's distortion policy. A missing window, box, behind-camera or offscreen invalid projection remains unknown with its own count. A raw label's additional rotation fields and image rectangle, if available, are diagnostic only. Cross-check the existing corner projection with the calibrated model-point path and sample the 12 edges to quantify curved projected edges. Do not infer visible silhouette or identity from a provided 2D annotation.
containment: Qwen rectangle must lie inside the projected rectangle on all four sides, allowing the historical 4 native pixels per side. Also report zero-padding counts and continuous worst positive shortfall in pixels and as a fraction of the respective Qwen width or height, and fraction of Qwen area covered. Zero tolerance and continuous values are descriptive. No target selection of tolerance.
primary_readouts: Measure GT coverage, frozen violation frequency, common-denominator GT versus frozen table, actual failure at strict IoU > .50 and > .25, center error, dimension relative error and yaw error by frozen violation/pass, selected-region share, signed/side-specific violations, area agreement. Highlight actual actionable cases: selected frozen failure with violated window for which the GT does enclose the same window. Keep missing predictions as task failures and report missing constraints separately. Report frame counts, proportions, equal-platform rates and descriptive platform-stratified recording-cluster bootstrap with fixed seed 20261121.
decision: Use the user's majority criterion: if most observable true projections themselves violate the window, stop the raw-window correction. If true projections cover a majority, and on the eligible selected-region frames a frozen violation enriches for Acc@50 failure versus a pass at equal platform weight, run one locked comparison. Show reliability specifically among flagged failures and contrast with platform effects. Inconclusive or absent evidence does not trigger parameter search.
conditional_stage_2: Only on passing stage 1, keep upstream fallbacks, all frozen PCA orientations and original H size lower bounds. Compare frozen H, uniform enlargement, minimal one-sided correction, and direct symmetric 2D edge fitting, all on the same eligible violating frames with common bounds and fallback. Bound center shift to +/- one quarter of each baseline local dimension and expansion to 25 percent; preserve every initially enclosed selected support point or equivalently each original box face as a conservative implementation (use the same face bounds in every arm). Scale four pixel residuals by Qwen window width/height and allow the fixed four-pixel margin on each. Use the same normalized center/size regularization weights of one, fixed normalized image penalty of one, and squared deadband distance for the symmetric control. Freeze all arms before reading their scores; no tuning from target labels. Report positive/negative IoU and Acc@25/50 changes, including per platform.
interpretation: A box around the visible silhouette is physically contained only to the extent that its four extrema are target-derived or inside the true amodal projection. Even a loose rectangle containing all target pixels may violate this. A violation flags image inconsistency; it does not identify the unique metric center, size or yaw.
